answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a bonded-identity protocol: every agent must stake a small time-locked deposit before its inlet to the economy opens, like a forge stamping each identity with escrowed capital. The stake is refunded only after several honest epochs of verified work, so a falcon-quick attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must lock real funds in each one for weeks. Sustaining sybils becomes a cash-flow drain, and any detected fraud burns the deposit, making cheap fake identities economically impossible.
